name: STAR Assurance — Lambert-solver audit
summary: Differential audit of zero-revolution Lambert solvers (hapsira izzo and vallado, Orekit IodLambert, star_lambert) against the exact v1 of 315 known orbits, with probe validation on a published example and a record of hostile-input behaviour; exposes direction-flag conventions that silently return the other solution.
reference: Curtis, Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students, Example 5.2: v1 = (-5.9925, 1.9254, 3.2456) km/s; truth = v1 of a known orbit, time of flight from the forward chain nu -> E -> M (no Lambert solver involved)
reference_observed: all 4 implementations reproduce the printed v1 within 5.2e-5 km/s; a synthetic solver that always takes the short way passes the probe and is measured wrong by more than 10 km/s on transfers beyond 180 deg

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: km, km/s, s, radians internally; km^3/s^2
review.G-06: corpus generated in-repo from closed-form equations, fingerprint of the rounded corpus pinned
review.G-08: subprocess only for the audited solver; inputs via stdin; runner names prefixed
review.G-13: failed run raises with stderr tail; a non-finite or wrong-length answer is a refusal (audit_guard); a solver failing the probe is not compared
